notes: Every test is phrased so that 'Yes' means the vendor is compatible with Plum. 'legacy' lists the v1 41-question ids this test replaces. 'risk' = a 'No' or 'Open' here needs an engineering escalation (platform/base-class gap), not just a vendor question. 'platform' says which part of the Xoxoday merchandise stack (see /merch-sensei) consumes the answer.

gate.item: Order placement contract is complete: documented request schema, vendor order id in the response, sync/async behaviour stated, and the address schema maps to our shipping fields.
Orders are idempotent: our reference is accepted, a duplicate never creates a second order, and a timed-out order can be looked up by our reference.
Order status is complete and mappable: enumerated statuses, every one maps to our six delivery statuses, an order-details lookup exists, and updates arrive by webhook or polling.
Shipment tracking (carrier plus tracking number or URL) is returned via API after dispatch.
Serviceability of the regions/pincodes we need is confirmed, with documented behaviour for non-serviceable addresses.
A returns, replacement or refund path exists for damaged, wrong or undelivered items.
A reconciliation source of truth exists that carries our reference per line.
Catalogue identifiers are stable and accepted unchanged by Place Order.
Transport and authentication are secure and documented.

tests.test: The documentation covers the full order lifecycle the integration needs: catalogue, place order, order status/details, tracking and reconciliation. A catalogue-only doc fails.
tests.pass: Every lifecycle stage has at least one documented endpoint.
tests.platform: Scopes the whole connector (merch-sensei Phase 1 batches 3 to 6).

tests.test: Every endpoint has a complete request and response example, not a truncated screenshot.
tests.platform: Fixtures for contract and unit tests.

tests.test: Enumerated and coded fields are explained (for example status 1/2, visibility 1-4, type_id values).
tests.pass: Each enum value has a meaning.

tests.test: The document is dated, versioned and names an owner.
Authentication method is documented (API key, Basic, OAuth2, HMAC, JWT or session) with the exact header name, format and an example request.
tests.pass: Method, header name/format and a sample authenticated request are all present.
tests.platform: getReqHeaders(). Custom header names must be added to vendorCallLogger.mongo.redactHeaders or credentials leak into Mongo logs.

tests.test: For token auth: token endpoint, grant type, request body and token lifetime (expiry field) are documented and work on staging. NA for static keys.
tests.pass: Token call returns a token plus an expiry value; TTL is stated.
tests.platform: fetchAccessToken() + /vendor/updateAccessToken scheduler; token stored in the tokens table.

tests.test: Expired or revoked token response is documented (401, 403 or a custom code) and refresh behaviour is stated.
tests.pass: Specific status/code for expiry is documented and reproduced on staging.
tests.platform: errorHandler() and the token refresh scheduler cadence.

tests.test: Invalid credentials return a documented error (4xx JSON), not 200 with an error body or an HTML page.
tests.pass: Bad key/secret gives 401/403 with JSON error body.
tests.platform: Base errorHandler handles 401/403; a 200-with-error would be stored as a success.

tests.test: If requests are signed (HMAC), the algorithm, exact string-to-sign, timestamp/nonce tolerance and a worked example are documented. NA if not used.
tests.pass: A worked example lets us reproduce the signature byte for byte.

tests.test: Credential rotation process is documented, ideally with two keys valid at once for zero-downtime rotation.
tests.pass: Rotation steps and overlap window stated.

tests.test: IP allowlisting requirement (if any) and how to submit our egress IPs per environment are documented.
tests.pass: Requirement stated either way; process given if required.

tests.test: Separate staging/sandbox and production base URLs and credentials exist and are clearly separated.
tests.pass: Both base URLs listed; staging reachable with staging credentials.

tests.test: Sandbox catalogue is representative of production (same fields, comparable products and pricing), and test products are listed.
tests.pass: Parity stated or differences documented; test SKUs given.
tests.platform: Contract test fixtures and smoke test.

tests.test: Sandbox can drive an order through every lifecycle status (confirm, ship, deliver, cancel, return) or trigger test webhooks.
tests.pass: A documented way to move test orders between statuses.
tests.platform: Staging smoke test: merchandise_vendor_order_details must move 1 -> 2 -> 3 and cancel must refund.

tests.test: Onboarding prerequisites (contract, KYB, deposit) and lead time to production keys are documented.
Supported countries and currencies are listed.
tests.platform: Central vendor row: supports_currency_in_api, default_product_currency (missing row = OPM00075).

tests.test: Sandbox/test orders are never physically shipped or billed, and the way to mark or cancel a test order in production is documented.
tests.platform: Safe staging run and production smoke test.

tests.test: A product list endpoint exists with method, path and filter parameters (country, category, currency).
tests.pass: Endpoint documented and returns products on staging.
tests.platform: productListingConfigs + getVendorProducts(); without it products are created manually in karma.

tests.test: Pagination method (page, offset or cursor) is documented with a reliable end-of-list signal (total count or next cursor).
tests.pass: We can loop every page and know when we are done.
tests.platform: getVendorProducts() must fetch all pages; sync TRUNCATEs the table first.

tests.test: Each sellable item has a stable unique identifier (SKU or variant id) that Place Order accepts unchanged.
tests.pass: The id in the catalogue response is the id in the order request; it does not change between syncs.
tests.platform: sku must be deterministic and reversible into the vendor's order identifiers (api_product_name = sku).

tests.test: Product response schema documents name, price, currency, image, description, brand and an active flag with its active value.
tests.platform: {model}_products columns; brand is required by the karma listing.

tests.test: Variants (size, colour) structure is documented and it is clear which ids the order API needs for a variant.
tests.pass: Variant nesting and the order-time variant id are explicit. NA if no variants.
tests.platform: formatProductResponse(): one sku per variant, reversible.

tests.test: Stock or availability is returned per item/variant, or a stock-check endpoint exists.
tests.pass: Stock field or endpoint documented and returned on staging.

tests.test: Availability freshness is stated, and an out-of-stock-at-order-time failure has its own documented error.
tests.pass: Freshness stated and a specific OOS error code exists.
tests.platform: errorHandler(); order fails cleanly instead of later cancellation.

tests.test: Catalogue changes (new items, delistings, price changes) are pushed by webhook, or the recommended polling frequency is stated.
tests.pass: Either a product webhook or a stated sync cadence.

tests.test: A failing catalogue page returns a non-2xx status, never an empty 200 that looks like the end of the list.
tests.pass: Forced failure (bad page or auth) returns an error status.
tests.platform: A silent empty page makes the sync disable every product it did not see (rule: catalog sync fails loudly).

tests.test: Catalogue size and maximum page size are stated.
Pricing model is stated: fixed price per SKU or open amount.
tests.platform: vendorType fixedSku (needs skuTable and karma Variant B) vs variableSku.

tests.test: Category, warranty/T&C, usage notes and country of availability are provided per product.
tests.platform: vendor_tables.php columns categories, terms_conditions, how_to_use, country.

tests.test: Image URLs are HTTPS, stable and publicly reachable (no expiring signed URLs).
Per-product order constraints are documented: max quantity, mandatory recipient fields (phone, email), region restrictions.
tests.pass: Constraints listed per product or globally.

tests.test: Incremental sync is supported (filter by updated_at or a changes feed).
tests.platform: Cheaper sync than full TRUNCATE + reload.

tests.test: Custom attributes (brand, image, description, category) are mapped to named fields, or the attribute codes to read are listed.
tests.platform: formatProductResponse() field mapping (Magento custom_attributes, Shopify metafields).

tests.test: The catalogue price is the amount we are charged, or the breakdown (tax, shipping, handling, discount) is documented.
tests.pass: Landed cost is computable from the API.

tests.test: Currency codes are ISO 4217 and map to our wallet currency without manual conversion.
tests.pass: ISO codes and billing currency stated.

tests.test: Price change policy is stated: notice period, and what happens if the price changed between sync and order (reject, or charge new price).
Shipping charges and taxes (GST/VAT) per order are documented: included in price or charged separately per region.
A balance endpoint exists and returns the real-time prepaid balance. NA if the account is postpaid/credit.
tests.pass: Endpoint returns balance and currency on staging.

tests.test: Balance scope (global vs per currency/market) is stated and matches how we fund the account.
tests.platform: Balance module returns vendorData per currency.

tests.test: An order with insufficient balance is rejected up front with a specific documented error, before any fulfilment.
tests.pass: Distinct error code; no order created.

tests.test: Funding model (prepaid, credit line, invoice) and low-balance alerts are documented.
Place Order is documented with method, path and the full request schema: required/optional flags, types and max lengths.
tests.pass: Schema complete and a staging order succeeds using only the docs.

tests.test: A successful order response contains the vendor order id in a named field.
tests.pass: Field named in docs and present on staging.
tests.platform: formatOrderResponse() must return apiOrderId and code = {model}_vendor_{apiOrderId}; no id means throw.

tests.test: The full success response schema is documented (every field we must store), not only a happy-path example.
Sync vs async is stated: is the order confirmed in the response, or pending and confirmed later by webhook/poll?
Every vendor-required address/recipient field can be filled from our shipping fields (first/last name, address 1/2, city, state/zone, country, postcode, contact number, email).
Formats are stated for country (ISO2/ISO3/name), state (code/name), phone (E.164 or local) and postcode.
Max length per address field and the behaviour on overflow (truncate or reject) are documented.
Optional fields are stated: empty last name, empty address line 2, optional email.
tests.platform: Fallbacks (Dpanda: first name for empty last name, recipientMobileNumber for empty contact).

tests.test: Quantity > 1 and multi-line orders are documented, including whether the vendor order id is per order or per line.
tests.platform: maxCardsPerRequest; one order_product per vendor call.

tests.test: Recipient communications are documented: whether the vendor emails/SMSes the recipient, and if it can be disabled or white-labelled.
tests.platform: Avoid duplicate/unbranded notifications (we send status emails).

tests.test: Maximum synchronous response time is documented and is 120 seconds or less; slower processing is async.
tests.pass: Stated limit <= 120s and observed on staging.

tests.test: Invalid SKU, out-of-stock item and invalid address each return a distinct documented error.
tests.pass: Three negative calls, three distinct codes.

tests.test: It is stated whether an accepted order can later fail BEFORE confirmation, and how that is signalled. Yes = it cannot, or it is signalled as a cancel status.
tests.pass: Pre-confirmation failure path is explicit and maps to CANCELED.
tests.platform: Async pre-confirm failure is a base-class gap: escalate before building.

tests.test: Serviceability is checkable before or at order time (pincode check endpoint or immediate rejection), and the regions we need are covered.
tests.pass: Serviceability check documented; our target pincodes confirmed.

tests.test: Responsibility for address validation is stated (vendor validates vs our responsibility), with the error returned for a bad address.
Gift handling is supported: price-free packing slip/invoice, gift message.
Address or recipient changes after placement are supported or explicitly not supported.
Peak volume capacity is stated (orders per day/hour for bulk reward campaigns).
A client reference (PO number) field is accepted on Place Order and returned in order details, webhooks and reports.
tests.platform: externalOrderId = voucher_insert_id; webhook lookup by insert_id.

tests.test: Re-sending the same reference never creates a second order; it returns the original order or a specific duplicate error.
tests.platform: errorHandler(): 'order already exists' -> callVendorRefetch(); plus VI duplicate guard OPM00063.

tests.test: After a timeout or 5xx on Place Order, a documented way exists to check if the order was created (lookup by our reference) before retrying.
Reference constraints are stated: uniqueness scope (account/global, time window), max length and allowed characters.
tests.pass: Constraints stated and compatible with our numeric ids.

tests.test: An order is retrievable by our reference immediately after placement (or the consistency delay is documented).
tests.pass: Lookup right after create returns the order.

tests.test: The complete list of order status values is documented with the meaning of each.
tests.platform: webhookConfigs.orderStatus map; an unmapped status updates tracking only.

tests.test: Every vendor status maps unambiguously to PENDING, CONFIRMED, SHIPPED, DELIVERED, CANCELED or RETURNED (failed/rejected -> CANCELED).
tests.pass: status_map in answers covers every status with only these six targets.
tests.platform: Never ORDER_FAILED: unmapped on webhooks and crashes the polling loop.

tests.test: An order-details endpoint returns current status (and tracking) by vendor order id and/or our reference.
tests.platform: refetchOrderReqConfigs; fetchTrackingDetailsFromVendor() (needed when cached tracking is older than 1 day).

tests.test: An order-history endpoint lists orders over a date range with pagination.
Terminal statuses are defined, and the maximum time an order can stay pending/processing (or an auto-cancel rule) is stated.
tests.platform: Polling loop picks rows with status NOT IN (3,5); stuck orders poll forever.

tests.test: Partial or split shipments are documented: line-level vs order-level status.
Allowed status transitions are documented, including whether a status can move backwards.
tests.pass: State machine or transition list given.

tests.test: An unknown order id returns a documented not-found response (404 or code), not a 500.
Dispatch and delivery timestamps are returned in a documented format and timezone.
Push status webhooks exist. (Gate needs this or POL-01.)
A sample webhook payload is documented for each status event.
The webhook carries our reference and/or the vendor order id.
tests.platform: apiOrderId must equal merchandise_vendor_order_details.api_order_id (else look it up by insert_id).

tests.test: Webhook is a JSON POST body. Note whether it has a top-level 'data' key.
tests.platform: Non-JSON needs a dedicated plumAuth route (escalate). No top-level data -> add to api.integratedVendors.rawPayload.

tests.test: Webhook authenticity does not depend on a vendor signature we must verify (unsigned, IP allowlist, or signing optional).
tests.pass: Yes = no mandatory signature. Mandatory signature = No (escalate).
tests.platform: Vendor-signed webhooks need escalation before building.

tests.test: Payload is plain, or encrypted with AES over base64 with a null IV (the only supported scheme).
Webhook URL registration is documented (self-serve or via vendor, per environment).
Retry policy on non-2xx (count, backoff) and the response the vendor expects are documented.
tests.platform: plumAuth accepts even if VI fails downstream, so vendor retries will not fire: keep refetch/polling as backstop.

tests.test: Duplicate and out-of-order delivery is addressed (event id or event timestamp provided).
Webhook source IPs are published.
The shipped event includes tracking fields (carrier, tracking number, tracking URL).
tests.pass: Fields present in the shipped sample.
tests.platform: courier_tracking row; otherwise 'No courier tracking found'.

tests.test: Missed webhooks can be replayed or resent on request.
tests.platform: Recovery after plumAuth or VI outage.

tests.test: A status endpoint is suitable for scheduled polling (single or bulk). (Gate needs this or WHK-01.)
The status field name and response shape for polling are documented.
tests.platform: Base reads res['orders_status']; anything else needs an override.

tests.test: Allowed polling rate is stated, and a bulk status endpoint exists for many orders.
tests.pass: Rate stated; bulk available or volume acceptable.
tests.platform: Polling loop iterates every non-terminal row.

tests.test: Polling and webhook payloads share a shape, or both shapes are documented.
Carrier name and tracking number are returned via API after dispatch (not only on a portal or email).
tests.pass: Fields documented and present on a staging shipped order.

tests.test: A per-order customer tracking URL is returned.
Estimated delivery date is returned.
Multi-package shipments are represented (multiple tracking numbers, package/shipment ids).
tests.pass: Structure documented. NA if always single package.

tests.test: Shipping SLA (days to dispatch, days to deliver) is documented per region.
Proof of delivery (delivered timestamp, POD, receiver name) is available for disputes.
Vendor-side cancellation is signalled through a status (webhook/poll).
A client-initiated cancel API exists, with the allowed window.
tests.platform: Informational: our platform has no outbound cancel; ops handle it manually.

tests.test: Returns/replacement/refund process for damaged, wrong or undelivered items is documented with a window.
tests.platform: Ops process; RETURNED sets status 10 and emails but does NOT auto-refund.

tests.test: Undeliverable / return-to-origin (RTO) handling is documented: status sent, re-delivery attempts, and credit back to us.
tests.platform: Maps to RETURNED or CANCELED; refund implication differs.

tests.test: Refund mechanism and timeline are stated (credit to prepaid balance or credit note).
Replacements are linked to the original order (same id or a documented link).
Liability for items lost or damaged in transit is stated (who bears the cost, claim window).
A settlement/payment report or transaction ledger exists (API or scheduled file).
Each report line carries our reference and the vendor order id.
tests.pass: Both fields in the report schema.

tests.test: Report granularity and amount fields are documented: charged amount, tax, shipping, discount, currency, date.
The delay between order completion and appearing in the report is stated.
Refunds, cancellations, RTO and partial fulfilment appear in the same report, linked to the original order.
Tax invoices (GST-compliant where applicable) are provided per order or per period, with a download/API.
Report format (JSON/CSV), date-range filters and timezone are documented.
An error catalogue lists HTTP status, error code and meaning per endpoint.
tests.platform: errorHandler() mapping to existing OPM000xx ids.

tests.test: Error responses use one consistent JSON structure across all endpoints.
tests.pass: Same keys on every negative call.

tests.test: Failures use proper HTTP status codes (no 200 with success:false), or that pattern is explicitly documented.
tests.pass: Non-2xx on failure, or documented exception.

tests.test: Rate limits per endpoint and the over-limit response (429 + Retry-After) are documented.
Retry/backoff guidance is given, including which errors are safe to retry.
tests.platform: OPMS retry; never blind-retry Place Order.

tests.test: Uptime SLA, status page and maintenance notification process are published.
Recommended client timeouts per endpoint are stated.
Responses include a request/correlation id for support tickets.
All endpoints are HTTPS only (TLS 1.2+).
tests.pass: https base URLs; plain http refused.

tests.test: Recipient PII handling is documented: retention, purpose limitation, deletion on request; DPA available.
Credentials are sent in headers, never in query strings.
tests.platform: Keeps secrets out of URL logs.

tests.test: Cross-border orders: customs, duties, HS codes and who pays are documented. NA if domestic only.
Orders are fully prepaid: no cash-on-delivery or payment collection from the recipient.
Restricted items (batteries, liquids, regulated goods) and their shipping restrictions by region are documented.
Credentials are delivered through a secure channel per environment and are NOT embedded in the API document or screenshots.
tests.pass: No live secrets in the doc. A doc with secrets = No: ask the vendor to rotate them.
tests.platform: Credential hygiene; run scripts/scan_secrets.py on every doc.

tests.test: The integration credential is least-privilege (scoped to the resources we call), not an admin-level token.
tests.platform: Limits blast radius if our keys leak.

tests.test: A named integration/technical contact and escalation matrix exist.
Production incident response time is documented.
API versioning (URL or header) and a deprecation notice period are documented.
A changelog is published.
A Postman collection or OpenAPI spec is provided.
tests.platform: Enables the live staging run (Postman CLI).
